open_issues: Departure from the plan: the plan kept an `in_flight` map of claimed items for the path check. I replaced it with the unfinished items of the running batch (`batch`, `begun` and `done` sets in `State`). A claimed-only map misses queued items of the running batch that a later item could clash with.

Second departure: the pump waits until every job of the running batch has started (`begun`). Without this, a read made ahead could take money a starting job had not yet held; the budget test failed that way before the fix. It also means a batch with more items than workers reads nothing ahead until its last item starts.
Third departure: the pump needs the budget to fit a read plus a run, not a read cap alone, so nothing is read that could not then be run (the drain's existing rule for starting a job).

Scope question: the disjoint-paths rule is copied into drain.rs because plan.rs keeps `overlap`, `disjoint` and `SHARED_APPEND_ONLY` private and is outside the three allowed files. `read_ahead_paths_rule_matches_the_plan_grouping` checks the copy against `Plan::build`. A follow-up could make the rule `pub` in plan.rs and call it from both places.

`RealSteps` still keeps `read_ahead() == 0`, `plan_ahead() == None` and the default `recheck` and `reread`. Planning has no planning-only entry point in `Athena`, and a safe re-read of an already-read job does not exist. Build job 10 (wiring `[drain.pipeline]` into main.rs) needs both.
A reading made ahead that fails or is not runnable is dropped with a note and the worker reads again, so a failing read can be paid for twice.
Readings made ahead and never used (the run ended first) were paid for. The drain reports each in a note, and `read_ahead` caps how many there can be.
mistakes: The first version of the pump checked the budget before the running batch's own job had held its money. In the budget test it read ahead and starved the job it was meant to run beside. I caught it when the test failed and added the 'every job of the running batch has started' rule.
I did not run the full workspace `cargo test`; I ran the athena-cli package suite and left the workspace run to Athena's checks, as the brief allows.
learnings: `Drain` and `State` are shared across worker threads behind one Mutex, and `take_until_done` is the only worker loop (serial and parallel both use it). The new `Condvar` and State fields are therefore touched in the serial path too, but they do nothing there.
plan.rs groups two items into one group exactly when `disjoint` holds, so `Plan::build` can verify a copy of the rule from outside the crate.

A fake's counter measured at the moment a read starts can race with the drain's bookkeeping between a worker claiming an item and the fake logging that run. The gauge `reads started - runs ended` is race-free because a batch ends only after its runs return.
This shell cannot read cargo output saved to a file outside the working directory, so a large test run's per-test lines could not be inspected. Use a filter or `--lib` to keep the output short.
Plan::build orders ready items by effective priority, then rung, then age, and puts disjoint ones in the same group. An item with no touched paths gets its own group.
desires: A way to read the per-test lines of a large cargo test output without a pipe or a file outside the working directory.
A `pub` disjoint-paths function in athena-core's plan.rs, so the drain would not need a copy of the rule.
